Sample.evidence_source: [/page/4/Text/2] Of the 70 children who initially exceeded the 19 point cut off on the CDI, 33 were identified as being within the clinical range of depression using the CDRS-R. Thus, 33 children out of the total number of 380 assessed were considered to exhibit depressive symptomatology.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/8] This allowed conformity with DSM-III-R criteria for a Major Depressive Episode which state that symptoms must be of at least two weeks duration. Children exceeding a score of 40, which is recommended as [/page/4/Text/2] the score required for a child to be diagnosed as depressed (Poznanski, Mokros, Grossman and Freeman, 1985), were then selected as subjects.

Source.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/7] All children whose parents consented (no parents refused permission) completed the Children's Depression Inventory {(CDI) Kovaks, 1985] on a class basis. The questionnaire was read out to younger children and those whose reading was poor. [/page/3/Text/8] To further validate the levels of depression experienced by the children identified by the CDI, each child exceeding the cut-off score was individually interviewed two weeks later using the Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R; Poznanski, Grossman, Buchsbaum, Banegas, Freeman and Gibbons, 1984).
